# Spec: Note sharing

Spec ID: SPEC-01
Status: draft
Supersedes: —

## Problem & user

The notes API today serves only personal notes: a caller can list, create and delete their own notes, and nothing else. A user who wants another person to see a note has no way to do so through the API and must copy the content out by hand, which leaves the copy stale the moment the original changes. The request is that users can share notes with others.

## Goals / Non-goals

**Goals**

- A note owner can give a specific other user access to one of their notes without handing over ownership.
- A recipient can find and read the notes shared with them.
- Access stays exclusive: nobody other than the owner and the recipients the owner chose can read a note, and only the owner can delete it.
- An owner can see and withdraw the access they granted (subject to OQ-5).

**Non-goals**

- Transferring ownership of a note.
- Collaborative or real-time editing; the API has no note-update operation today (see Inputs and provenance), and edit access is undecided (OQ-2).
- Notifying recipients by email, push or in-app message (proposed; see OQ-10).
- Sharing groups, teams or organisations; sharing is per user (proposed; depends on OQ-1).
- Re-sharing by a recipient.

## User stories

- US-1: As a note owner, I want to share one of my notes with another user, so that they can read it without me copying its content.
- US-2: As a recipient, I want to list and open the notes shared with me, so that I can read them in the same API I use for my own notes.
- US-3: As a note owner, I want to see who a note is shared with and withdraw access, so that I stay in control of who can read it.
- US-4: As a user who was not given access, I want to be unable to learn a note's content, so that other users' notes stay private (this protects every owner).

## Acceptance criteria (EARS)

### Granting access

- [ ] AC-1 WHEN the owner of a note submits a share request for that note naming a recipient, the API shall grant that recipient [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: read-only access, or read and write access? — OQ-2] to the note.
- [ ] AC-2 A share request shall identify the recipient by [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: user ID, email address, or is sharing done through a public link with no named recipient? — OQ-1].
- [ ] AC-3 IF a caller who is not the owner of a note submits a share request for that note, THEN the API shall reject the request with [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found? — OQ-6].
- [ ] AC-4 IF a share request names a recipient who does not exist, THEN the API shall reject the request with [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: which status and message, given that a distinct response reveals whether a user exists? — OQ-7].
- [ ] AC-5 IF a share request is rejected, THEN the API shall leave the set of recipients of that note unchanged.

### Recipient access

- [ ] AC-6 WHEN a recipient requests a note shared with them, the API shall return [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: the note's current content (live), or the content as it was when shared (snapshot)? — OQ-11].
- [ ] AC-7 WHEN a recipient requests the notes shared with them, the API shall return them [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: inside the existing GET /notes response marked as shared, or through a separate listing? — OQ-4].
- [ ] AC-8 IF a caller who is neither the owner nor a recipient of a note requests that note, THEN the API shall respond with [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found? — OQ-6].
- [ ] AC-9 The API shall exclude a note's content from every response to a caller who is neither its owner nor one of its recipients.
- [ ] AC-10 IF a recipient requests deletion of a note shared with them, THEN the API shall leave the note in place.

### Managing and ending access

- [ ] AC-11 WHEN the owner of a note requests that note's recipients, the API shall return the list of users the note is shared with. [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: are listing and revoking recipients in scope for this spec? — OQ-5]
- [ ] AC-12 WHEN the owner of a note revokes a recipient's access, the API shall treat that user as neither owner nor recipient (AC-8) on every later request for the note. [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: are listing and revoking recipients in scope for this spec? — OQ-5]
- [ ] AC-13 WHEN the owner deletes a shared note, the API shall answer every later request for that note by a former recipient as in AC-8.

## Edge cases

- The owner shares a note with themself: undecided whether this is rejected or ignored (OQ-13). No criterion yet.
- The owner shares the same note with the same recipient twice: undecided whether the second request is idempotent or an error (OQ-12). No criterion yet. AC-5 still holds if it is rejected.
- A recipient's access is revoked while they hold an earlier response: the earlier response is not recalled; only later requests are denied (AC-12).
- A shared note is deleted: former recipients get the same response as a stranger (AC-13, AC-8).
- A non-recipient guesses a note ID: the response must not reveal the content (AC-9). Whether it reveals that the note exists depends on OQ-6.
- The recipient count limit is reached: the share request is rejected (NFR-1) and the recipient set is unchanged (AC-5).

## Non-functional requirements

- NFR-1: IF a share request would give a note more than [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: maximum recipients per note? — OQ-8] recipients, THEN the API shall reject it.
- NFR-2: WHEN access to a note is granted or revoked, the API shall [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: log the event (note ID, owner ID, recipient ID, timestamp, no note content), or not log it? — OQ-9].
- NFR-3: Accessibility and localisation: none apply. This is an HTTP API with no UI, and the repository has no message catalog.

## Inputs and provenance

**Data inputs**

| Input | Source | Trusted? | Freshness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Caller identity | Authentication of the API caller (mechanism not present in the repository; OQ-3) | Only after authentication | Per request |
| Note ID in a share, read, revoke or delete request | API caller | No | Per request |
| Recipient identifier in a share request | API caller | No | Per request |
| Note content returned to a recipient | Database, written earlier by the note owner (another user) | No (for the recipient) | Live or snapshot per OQ-11 |
| Set of recipients of a note | Database, written by this feature | Yes | Live |

**Requirement provenance**

- The core ability to share notes (US-1, US-2, AC-1, AC-6, AC-7) comes from the request: "Users should be able to share notes."
- The existing API serves only "the caller's notes", with no read-one or update route: `src/notes/routes.ts:2` (`GET /notes` lists the caller's notes), `src/notes/routes.ts:3` (`POST /notes`), `src/notes/routes.ts:4` (`DELETE /notes/:id`). These lines are the basis for AC-7's question, AC-10, AC-13, the edit-access Non-goal and OQ-2's default.
- The project scope is personal notes and specs live in `docs/specs/`: `AGENTS.md:3`.
- The access-exclusivity criteria (AC-3, AC-8, AC-9, AC-10, AC-12) and US-3/US-4 are inferred from what sharing means: access is granted without transferring ownership. The status codes stay open (OQ-6).
- No users, authentication or storage module exists in the repository. Every statement about users and identity rests on the caller concept at `src/notes/routes.ts:2`.

## Untrusted inputs

- **Caller identity.** Threat: a spoofed identity used to read or share another user's note. Neutralised by AC-3, AC-8 and AC-9, provided identity is authenticated. The mechanism is open as OQ-3.
- **Note ID.** Threat: enumerating or guessing IDs to read notes that were not shared (insecure direct object reference). Neutralised by AC-8 and AC-9. The existence leak depends on OQ-6.
- **Recipient identifier.** Threat: probing which users or email addresses exist (user enumeration), and malformed or oversized values. Partly covered by AC-4 (open as OQ-7) and AC-5. The size and format limit is not yet covered; it is part of OQ-7.
- **Note content shown to a recipient.** Threat: content written by one user is now delivered to another, so script or markdown injection hits any client that renders it. Not neutralised by a criterion. It is open as OQ-14.

## Open questions

- OQ-1: How does an owner name who to share with: a user ID, an email address, or a public link with no named recipient? — default if unanswered: an existing user's ID; public links are out of scope — blocks: AC-2
- OQ-2: What access does a recipient get: read-only, or read and write? — default if unanswered: read-only, because the API has no note-update operation even for owners (`src/notes/routes.ts:1-5`) — blocks: AC-1
- OQ-3: How is the caller authenticated? The repository has no auth code, yet `GET /notes` returns "the caller's notes". — default if unanswered: reuse whatever identifies the caller for `GET /notes` today — blocks: none
- OQ-4: Do shared notes appear in the existing `GET /notes` response (marked as shared) or in a separate listing? — default if unanswered: a separate listing, so `GET /notes` keeps meaning "the caller's own notes" — blocks: AC-7
- OQ-5: Are listing a note's recipients and revoking access in scope for this spec? — default if unanswered: yes, both — blocks: AC-11, AC-12
- OQ-6: What status does a caller get for a note they cannot access (non-owner share attempt, stranger read)? — default if unanswered: 404 Not Found in both cases, so note existence is not revealed — blocks: AC-3, AC-8
- OQ-7: What does a share request naming a non-existent recipient return, and what format and size limits apply to the recipient identifier? — default if unanswered: 400 with a generic "recipient not found" message; identifier at most 254 characters — blocks: AC-4
- OQ-8: What is the maximum number of recipients per note? — default if unanswered: 50 — blocks: NFR-1
- OQ-9: Are grant and revoke events logged? — default if unanswered: yes, with note ID, owner ID, recipient ID and timestamp, never note content — blocks: NFR-2
- OQ-10: Should recipients be notified when a note is shared with them? — default if unanswered: no, out of scope (listed as a Non-goal) — blocks: none
- OQ-11: Does a recipient see the note's current content (live) or the content at share time (snapshot)? — default if unanswered: live — blocks: AC-6
- OQ-12: Is sharing the same note with the same recipient twice idempotent or an error? — default if unanswered: idempotent success, no duplicate recipient — blocks: none
- OQ-13: Is an owner sharing a note with themself rejected or ignored? — default if unanswered: rejected with 400 — blocks: none
- OQ-14: Does the API sanitise or escape note content before returning it to a recipient, or is safe rendering the client's responsibility? — default if unanswered: the API returns content unchanged as JSON and the spec states that clients must render it as untrusted text — blocks: none

## Changelog

- 2026-10-21 · draft — created: US-1–US-4, AC-1–AC-13, NFR-1–NFR-3, OQ-1–OQ-14 — initial draft from the request "Users should be able to share notes."

**Non-goals**

- Sharing with groups, teams or through public or anonymous links. The request only covers one user named by email.

- US-2: As a recipient of a shared note, I want to access that note through the API, so that I can see what the owner shared with me.
